# National Geographic Education

> > K-12 educational resources from National Geographic Society covering earth science, oceanography, geography, ecology, and environmental conservation through case studies, lesson plans, and explorer profiles.

This site provides standards-aligned educational materials for prekindergarten through 8th grade, featuring interactive activities, GIS technology lessons, and real-world case studies from National Geographic explorers. Resources emphasize environmental science, indigenous communities, biodiversity conservation, and geographic literacy.

## Key Topics

- National Geographic Society
- Earth Science
- Ocean Conservation
- Ecology and Biodiversity
- Environmental Impact
- Indigenous Communities
- Deforestation and Rainforest Conservation
- Geographic Information Systems (GIS)
- Oceanography
- Case Studies
- Educational Resources (K-8)
- Seasonal Science
- Marine Protected Areas
- Amazon Rainforest
- Climate and Environmental Change

## Earth and Environmental Science

- [Oceanography](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/oceanography): Multidisciplinary ocean science covering climate, pollution, marine life
- [Volcanoes](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/volcanoes): Encyclopedic entry on volcanic eruptions, magma, and geological processes
- [Seasons](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/seasons): Teaching ideas and activities for seasonal education and observation
- [GIS (Geographic Information System)](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/geographic-information-system-gis/8th-grade): 8th grade intro to GIS technology, spatial data, and mapping applications

## Conservation and Ecology

- [Protect the Blue: Marine Protected Areas](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/protect-blue-marine-protected-areas): Grades 3-8 lesson comparing land vs ocean protected area percentages
- [Case Study: The Amazonian Road Decision](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/amazonian-road-decision/4th-grade): 4th grade case study on Pucallpa-Cruzeiro road impacts in Amazon rainforest
- [Coral Reef Fish Survey Simulation](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/coral-reef-fish-survey-simulation): Classroom activity simulating Belt Transect fish population surveys
- [TIL: The World's Largest Migration Isn't What You Think](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/til-worlds-largest-migration-isnt-what-you-think): Dr. Erika Montague explains diel vertical ocean migration phenomenon

## Geography and Human Societies

- [The History of Cities](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/history-cities/5th-grade): 5th grade lesson on urbanization from ancient Ur to modern megacities
- [Community Map](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/community-map): Pre-K to grade 2 introduction to maps and spatial concepts
- [We Are What We Eat](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/we-are-what-we-eat/5th-grade): 5th grade study of Hadza hunter-gatherers and traditional diets in Tanzania
- [Bering Land Bridge](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/bering-land-bridge): Map showing ancient human migration routes across North America

## Physical and Life Sciences

- [The Conservation of Matter During Physical and Chemical Changes](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/conservation-matter-during-physical-and-chemical-changes/4th-grade): 4th grade science on Law of Conservation of Mass and matter states
- [Receptor Sites](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/receptor-sites): Cell biology explanation of protein receptors and ligand binding

## National Geographic Explorers

- [Explorer At Work: Rachel Herring](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/explorer-at-work-rachel-herring): Choctaw researcher Rachel Herring studies energy transition in Japan
- [Modern Explorer | The Future of Penguins](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/future-penguins): Explorer Alizé Carrère studies king penguin behavior and ecology
- [Saving the Creeps](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/saving-creeps): Zoologist Lucy Cooke advocates for unloved species and biodiversity
- [Data Artist: Jer Thorp](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/data-artist-jer-thorp): Profile of Jer Thorp merging arts and data visualization

## Optional

- [Land Cover of the Chesapeake Bay](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/land-cover): EPA map showing Chesapeake Bay land cover from NLCD 2001 database
- [Rescue of Real-Life Robinson Crusoe](https://education.nationalgeographic.org/resource/rescue-real-life-robinson-crusoe/prekth-grade): Historical account of Alexander Selkirk's 1709 rescue after island survival
